caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 270 of 1994.
lawyer:
Golam Mohiuddin, Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioners. 
Not represented — The Respondents.
parties:
Serajul Islam & others ------ Petitioners
VS. 
Md Humayun Kabir and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: This petition for leave to appeal by the defendant-petitioners is from the judgment and order of a Division Bench of the High Court Division dated 27-3-94 in Civil Revision No. 1723 of 1992 making the Rule absolute and allowing the prayer of the plaintiff-respondents for ad interim injunction, which was disallowed both by the trial Court, the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla in Title Suit No. 46 of 1984 and on appeal by the 1st Court of Additional District Judge, Comilla in Miscellaneous Appeal No.15 of 1986. 

 2. The plaintiff-respondents filed the said title suit for partition. Their case was that the suit properties were the properties of Azimuddin and Md Hanif in equal shares. Azimuddin predeceased Hanif and the widow of Azimuddin was Nika married by Md. Hanif who managed the properties of both the two brothers. Md Hanif brought up the minor children of Azimuddin. The plaintiffs are the successive heirs of Azimuddin. Md. Hanif taking advantage of his position as the manager of his brother's properties after his death managed to record his same as the sole owner of the suit properties in CR and SA khatians. They prayed for temporary and ad interim injunction restraining the petitioners who were defendant Nos. 10 and 32-35 in the suit, from taking compensation money from the Land Acquisition Officer, respondent No. 23 and also restraining respondent No. 23 from making payment of compensation money for plot No. 21/4 measuring 0.44 acres of land in the suit. 

 3. Both the Courts below rejected the plaintiff-respondents prayer for temporary injunction on the ground that the plaintiff respondents could not make out any prima facie and arguable case by producing any evidence of ownership and possession of the land involved in the application. 

 4. The High Court Division was of the opinion that to establish a prima facie case it is not necessary to file documents or papers and it can be spelt out in the plaint and the Court can find out if the parties will go on trial on a fair and triable issue on a careful consideration of the pleadings. The Courts below did not take into consideration the fact that at the time of preparation of the khatians in question the elder brother Azimuddin was dead and the children of Azimuddin were under the care and custody of Md. Hanif. The High Court Division was therefore of the opinion that the plaintiff-respondents have a prima facie arguable case and, as such, allowed their prayer for ad interim injunction. 

 5. Mr. Golam Mohiuddin, learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners, submits that the High Court Division erred in law in importing a new concept with regard to an arguable prima facie case. He submits that the prima facie case is not only to be gathered from the pleading of the parties but also from the papers and documents that the parties may choose to file while arguing the injunction matter. A plaintiff may make any amount of tall claims in the plaint but if he cannot substantiate his claim by any evidence of any nature whatsoever during the hearing of temporary injunction matter then it cannot be said that he has a prima facie arguable case. 

 6. While we do not subscribe to the widely stated view of the High Court Division regarding arguable prima facie case we are not inclined to interfere with the ultimate order passed by it because it will avoid multiplicity of litigation and since the injunction is only in respect of withdrawal of compensation money for acquisition of land, we do not think that it will cause sufferings to either side if the matter is postponed while he partition suit is decided.
